extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, corporate communications officers, and publicists seeking wire-service pickup
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for writing and distributing press releases that meet AP/Reuters (wire service) editorial standards so they are eligible for pickup by major wire bureaus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-source verification required
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services require verification from more than one source for important claims; do not rely on single-party assertions for major facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named sources preferred
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible provide named sources rather than anonymous sourcing so facts can be checked and attributed; named sourcing increases credibility for wire pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose single-party sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose when information from single party
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information or a claim comes from a single party, explicitly disclose that fact rather than implying independent corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent verification of claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in a release should be subject to independent verification (documents, third-party sources, records) rather than only source assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Standards (Reuters Manual)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Simple, direct language which can be assimilated quickly, which goes straight to the heart of the matter, and in which, as a general rule, facts are marshalled in logical sequence according to their relative importance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain, direct prose; lead with the most important facts; organize information in logical order by importance so editors/readers can assimilate key points rapidly.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP/style standards
rubrics_metrics.description: AP Stylebook is American journalism standard; AP libel guidelines; AP state abbreviations; AP standardized writing conventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with AP style conventions (spelling, abbreviations, formats) and libel/legal guidance used by U.S. newsrooms to avoid copyediting friction or legal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction policies (Reuters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent about errors; Rectify promptly and clearly; Don't disguise or bury corrections in subsequent stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an error is discovered in a release or follow-up story, correct it openly and promptly rather than hiding or minimizing the correction; transparency maintains trust with wire editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality and objectivity (wire standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single objective news feed to all subscribers; Avoid overt partiality; Demonstrably correct information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services aim to distribute objective, non-partisan information. Releases should avoid partisan framing, overt advocacy, or material that can't be substantiated as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability (press release implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: All facts checkable; Multiple sources for major claims; Named sources where possible; Documents linked
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations, links to source documents/data files, and multiple corroborating sources for major claims so wire and downstream editors can verify quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (press release implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple, direct language; Logical sequence; Most important first; No marketing-speak
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon and promotional phrasing; structure the release so the lead contains the key news and subsequent paragraphs provide supporting detail in order of importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (press release implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: All names spelled correctly; All titles current; All dates accurate; All numbers verified
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meticulous fact-checking on names, titles, dates, statistics and numeric claims is essential — factual or typographical errors reduce chances of wire pickup and can propagate widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style compliance (press release implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: AP style throughout; Standard formatting; Professional appearance; No errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere consistently to a recognized newsroom style (AP recommended) and present the release in a clean, professional format with no typographical or grammatical mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality (press release implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: No partisan framing; No promotional language; Objective tone; Balanced presentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep language factual and balanced; avoid promotional superlatives, marketing slogans, or obvious advocacy that would make the piece read like advertising rather than news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services evaluate whether a release has real news value (timeliness, impact, novelty, relevance) rather than being routine marketing or self-promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefness / Brevity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep releases concise and focused; avoid long-winded background or extraneous material that buries the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor releases to the audience and geographic or topical scope; make clear why the story matters to the wire service's subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visuals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality images, videos, charts or other assets when appropriate; visuals increase pick-up likelihood and meet many wire requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (what wire services look for)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure headlines and ledes are unambiguous and the release leaves little room for misinterpretation by editors or readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (what wire services look for)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services prioritize verifiable facts; releases should enable quick confirmation of claims by editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get on the wire: Reg FD-compliant channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distribution methods that comply with regulatory disclosure obligations (e.g., Regulation Fair Disclosure) when releasing material that impacts investors or markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get on the wire: Major distribution services
rubrics_metrics.description: Use major distribution services (BusinessWire, PR Newswire)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ established wire distributors that have working relationships with AP/Reuters and can format and route releases in a newsroom-friendly way.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get on the wire: Direct relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct relationships with wire bureau chiefs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate direct contacts with wire editors and bureau staff; strong relationships can improve the odds of editorial attention or clarification when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get on the wire: Emerging distribution methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of newer channels that use AI to route or summarize releases; ensure such formats still meet verifiability and style expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style compliant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conform to AP stylebook conventions (spelling, abbreviation, punctuation) so copyeditors don't need to rework or reject the release for style reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: All facts verifiable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every factual assertion can be checked against a named source, document, dataset or public record; avoid unsubstantiated claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sources cited
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite more than one source for major claims whenever possible to satisfy newsroom verification standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language throughout
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon, marketing fluff, and complex sentence structures; use straightforward language that can be quickly understood by editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: No errors of fact, grammar, or spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: No errors of fact, grammar, or spelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully proofread and fact-check the release; even minor errors reduce credibility and the chance of wire pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical sequencing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize information so that the most important facts come first and supporting details follow in a coherent order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief but complete
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be succinct but include all essential facts editors need to report the story or to follow up for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visuals provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to appropriate visual assets (images, charts, video) in newsroom-ready formats and with proper captions/credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible identify the people or organizations providing key information to enable verification and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuinely newsworthy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the announcement offers a timely, impactful, or novel development rather than routine corporate promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral tone
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid promotional adjectives and advocacy language; present facts and allow journalists to interpret significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more than one trusted distribution path (e.g., major wire services plus direct outreach) to maximize reach and redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local angles for regional bureaus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include localized context or data where appropriate to increase relevance for regional wire bureaus and local editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoed appropriately
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using an embargo, follow accepted newsroom practices (clear embargo time, reason, and what is and isn't allowed) so editors can plan coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provided with documents/data files
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply source documents, datasets, regulatory filings or additional material that supports claims in the release and enables verification.
